Design decisions from Jack Heart (2026-11-22) on Fork #2 (server topology) and Fork #3 (page topology / report vs status):

"2: dont think this matters do much
3: we need to keep report as conceptually similar and something you can print after an experiment and potentialyl save in git. i would thik ti makes sense to build a single served webpage that combined two different components that can load async"

Key implications:
- Fork #2 (one process vs two processes on the same host) is not a major constraint; keep it clean and safe.
- Fork #3: Keep static `etude report` conceptually the same—a printable artifact you can produce after an experiment and potentially commit to git.
- For the served experiment page, combine the operational status component (jobs run/completed, what is running where, system metrics) and the `report()` component on ONE webpage where the two components load asynchronously (so neither blocks the other, rather than splitting them onto separate experiment vs `/report` pages).
